front: What is the relationship between Linux and a distribution such as Debian?
back: Linux is only the kernel. A distribution adds tools, a package manager, often a desktop, and an installer to make a whole system.

front: How do Windows, macOS and Linux differ in licensing?
back: Windows and macOS are proprietary, sold or tied to the vendor’s system. The Linux kernel and most distributions are open source and free to use and change.

front: Name two things that differ between Linux and Windows in everyday use.
back: Linux comes in many distributions, with several choices of desktop and package manager, and is run on servers mainly from the command line. Windows has one vendor and one desktop.

front: What is an ISO file, and how do you use it to install Linux?
back: An ISO is a single-file copy of an optical disc that holds the installer. Write it to a USB stick (or DVD), or attach it to a virtual machine, and boot from it.

front: What is the difference between an ISO and an operating system image?
back: An ISO is an installer you run once. An OS image is an already installed system that you copy to a disk or SD card and boot directly, such as a Raspberry Pi image or a cloud image.

front: Why should you check the checksum of a downloaded ISO?
back: The project publishes a checksum, and a match proves the file is not corrupt or tampered with. Also choose the right architecture (`amd64` for a PC, ARM for a Raspberry Pi).

front: Which part of an installation chooses what to load after power-on, and which is the usual Linux one?
back: The boot loader, usually GRUB. It runs first and loads the kernel, and it shows a menu on a dual-boot machine.
Two operating systems on one computer, and you choose one at every start. Only one runs at a time, unlike in a virtual machine where both run together.

front: Why would Jonas try Linux in a virtual machine first?
back: A virtual machine runs Linux as a program inside his current system, so his real disk is untouched and he can throw the VM away. The cost is that it shares the real machine’s memory and CPU.

front: What is WSL, and how does WSL 2 differ from WSL 1?
back: The Windows Subsystem for Linux runs a Linux environment on Windows with no dual boot. WSL 2 runs a real Linux kernel in a lightweight VM; WSL 1 translates Linux calls to Windows.
A virtual server you rent from a cloud provider by the hour. You pick a size, an OS image and a region, and it starts from the image without an installer.

front: Which tool applies your SSH key and accounts to a new cloud instance at first boot?
back: `cloud-init`. It reads the user data you supplied and can create users, add an SSH public key, set the hostname and install software.

front: How does Ada usually work on a Linux cloud instance?
back: She connects with SSH and uses the command line. Servers rarely have a desktop, because the command line needs less memory and can be scripted.

front: Compare a GUI with the command line on a Linux server.
back: A GUI uses windows and a mouse; the command line uses text commands. Servers are normally run from the command line: less memory, scriptable, works over a slow SSH link.

front: Is the desktop environment part of the distribution choice?
back: No, it is a separate choice. GNOME, KDE Plasma and Xfce are common, and a distribution usually offers several. Settings are changed in the desktop’s settings program.

front: What is the difference between a stable and a beta release?
back: A stable release is ready for production and gets only bug and security fixes. A beta is a pre-release for testing that may contain bugs, so keep it off the build server.

front: What is the difference between a fixed release and a rolling release?
back: A fixed release (Debian stable, Ubuntu) comes in versions now and then, while a rolling release (such as Arch) is updated continuously and has no big version jump.

front: Why must you plan an upgrade before a release’s support ends?
back: After the end of support there are no more security fixes. Ubuntu LTS releases get five years of updates and come every two years.
